source_context: Public LinkedIn discussion following participant acknowledgment of the initiating Human as the Interoperability Layer exchange.

observations.description: An initiating participant publicly described an informal exchange as becoming a conversation, research trace, paper, and public replication protocol.
A commenter characterized recurring AI-mediated writing patterns as a shared mask and later expanded the claim into a public post using the term slop.
The exchange identified cadence matching, vocabulary adaptation, and stylistic synchronization as possible mechanisms of successful communication rather than automatic evidence of degraded output.
The term slop was observed operating as a possible categorical judgment against machine-mediated work rather than an artifact-level quality determination.

A commenter argued that social relevance requires forcing society to take an opinion seriously, while the act of selecting and contesting the proposition itself supplied evidence of individual significance assignment and trace continuation.

next_empirical_work: Build a labeled corpus of human, model, and jointly revised responses.
Test probabilistic model-family and prompt-pattern classification with held-out samples.
Measure directional style accommodation over interaction time.
Separate participant-reported communication quality from surface similarity.
Test whether observers systematically rate equivalent content differently when origin labels change.
